summary: This article explains why old phones and other electronics hold valuable metals, how e-waste can harm the land when it is thrown away, how devices are recycled, and what students can do to help.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “Old Phones, New Treasure: Recycling Electronics” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: working by using electricity and tiny parts, like phones and computers
worth a lot of money or very useful
able to hurt people, animals, or nature

challengeTerms.def: something useful that people need, such as water, metal, or energy
to take something out, often with effort
poisonous and able to harm living things

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that an old phone in a drawer is just junk? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain the steps that turn an old phone into material for new products.
struggling: Pre-teach electronic, valuable, and harmful with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use resource, extract, and toxic in a short paragraph that explains one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
